criteria.check: Read metrics.py and graph.py draft node; every memo figure is a Metric computed in metrics.compute, the model only receives as_table output. Probed all nine synth cases.
Every Metric carries evidence ids; test_evidence_reproduces_each_figure recomputes M2,M5-M9,M11,M12,M14 from them. Traceability from the written memo artefact is a separate major finding.
Read draft(): user prompt is account name, period, metrics table and policy rule lines only; no transactions.
Probed guard.check with word numbers, word scales, unit/sign mismatches and policy thresholds; read redraft routing (MAX_REDRAFTS=2, test_hallucinating_model_is_caught_and_redrafted).
Read RULES; probed non-trading FPS credits (savings transfer, HMRC VAT repayment, capital injection): all categorised revenue_transfer.
Thresholds and outcomes are in YAML, but metrics.py hard-codes M10=99.0 when there is no debt and M15=0.0 for card-settled revenue, which decide R2/R7 policy outcomes in code.
Grepped repo for employer names, emails, sort codes; all statements generated by synth.py. One real company name used as a supplier (minor).

Read ingest.load_csv: missing columns, bad dates, non-finite amounts, balance breaks, duplicate/empty ids all raise StatementError; tests/test_ingest.py covers them. Probed newest-first and BOM files: refused (clear-ish errors).
Read ci.yml: no secrets, evals run --llm fake; get_llm defaults to fake. Ran pytest locally with no key: 94 passed.
Generated 9 cases x 39 seeds and compared M5 to truth; tests only use seed 7. Also noted M6 truth shares the code's (wrong) definition.
Probed guard with 'forty-eight thousand pounds', '30 thousand', '£12 [M1] million': all reported grounded.

findings.claim: When debt service is zero, M10 is a hard-coded 99.0 regardless of cash flow (dscr=inf at line 50). A loss-making business with no existing loans gets 'debt service cover 99.00' in the memo and passes the policy's only fail-level cash rule (R2 >= 1.25). New-to-credit applicants are common for working-capital facilities.
findings.repro: 12 months: CARD ACQUIRER SETTLEMENT +10000 on the 2nd, FRESHFIELD FOODS LTD DD -14000 on the 5th, opening 100000. metrics.compute -> M9=-48000.0, M10=99.0; policy.evaluate -> R2 'pass'. (scratchpad panel02/staff/probe1.py case A)

findings.claim: M10 is not a defensible DSCR proxy: the numerator adds back owner drawings (excluded from operating), so cash the owner took out counts as cover. A credit analyst deducts drawings for an owner-managed SME. It also covers existing debt only; the proposed facility's repayment is not in the denominator, and that is not written down as out of scope.
findings.repro: end=2026-09-30, seed 7: cafe/good M10=3.12 but (M9-M11)/M8=0.95; cafe/stretched 1.43 vs -0.74; ecommerce/stretched 1.36 vs -0.22. cafe/good is policy 'pass' while its cash after drawings does not cover its existing loan. (probe2.py)

findings.claim: M15 counterparty key is description words [2:5]. For two-word payer names it includes the invoice reference, so each invoice becomes its own 'counterparty' and concentration is understated. For card/gateway revenue it is 0.0 (line 59) and R7 auto-passes, while the memo template (llm.py:43) and policy text (policy/uk_sme_default.yaml:53) call it a share 'of inflows'; the committed example memo says the top payer is '0.0% [M15] of inflows' for a business whose inflows are 100% one acquirer.
findings.repro: 12 months of 'FPS CREDIT T WHITTAKER INV10nn' +9000 and 'FPS CREDIT ELMS DENTAL PRACTICE INV20nn' +1000: true top share 90%, M15=10.0, R7 pass. (probe1.py case B); examples/cafe_stretched.memo.md:5

findings.claim: M6 'Days overdrawn' counts dates on which some transaction left a negative balance, not days the account closed overdrawn; days with no transactions while overdrawn are not counted. The generator computes truth the same way (synth.py:220), so P1/tests cannot detect it. R4 (<15 days) can pass a month-long overdraft.
findings.repro: Opening 0; 2025-01-01 +100; 2025-01-02 -5000; 2025-01-28 +6000; one +100 credit per later month. Overdrawn 2-27 Jan (26 days); M6=1, R4 pass. (probe1.py case C)

findings.claim: M13 late VAT treats a payment as on time only if made in days 1-11 of Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct. HMRC deadlines are one month and seven days after the period end across three stagger groups, so on-time payments on a real statement are counted late (R5 refer). A business that pays no VAT at all scores 0 late and passes R5 'No late VAT payments'.
findings.repro: 12 months revenue plus HMRC VAT -3000 on 2025-02-07, 05-07, 08-07, 11-07 (on time for stagger 1) -> M13=4, R5 refer. Same statement with no VAT lines -> M12=0, M13=0, R5 pass. (probe1.py case D)

findings.claim: Bounced and re-presented direct debits are double counted. The original debit keeps its category (loan repayment / HMRC VAT), the 'UNPAID DD' reversal credit becomes returned_dd and lands in operating cash flow (metrics.py:46), and the re-presented debit is counted again. M8 debt service, M12 VAT paid and M13 are overstated, and M9 gains the reversal.
findings.repro: Monthly +10000 card, -1000 'DD BRIDGEPOINT FINANCE LOAN'; March: '+1000 UNPAID DD BRIDGEPOINT FINANCE LOAN' then re-presented -1000; May: HMRC VAT -3000, '+3000 UNPAID DD HMRC VAT', HMRC VAT -3000. Result M8=13000 (true 12000), M12=6000 (true 3000), M13=2, M10=9.08 (true 9.75). (probe3.py)

findings.claim: '^FPS CREDIT|^BACS CREDIT' classifies every inbound bank transfer as customer revenue. Transfers from the business's own savings account, HMRC VAT repayments and owner capital injections become revenue: an unidentified credit is guessed as revenue instead of falling to 'other'. This inflates M2, M3, M9 and M10.
findings.repro: 12 x card +10000 plus 'FPS CREDIT HARBOURSIDE SAVINGS ACCT' +50000, 'FPS CREDIT HMRC VAT REPAYMENT' +8000, 'FPS CREDIT MR J SMITH CAPITAL INJECTION' +20000 -> all revenue_transfer, M2=198000 vs trading revenue 120000. (probe1.py case E)

findings.claim: The guard only sees digits. Numbers in words pass, and so do word scales after a bare integer of 0-31 (the prose-integer exemption) or after a tagged metric value. Matching ignores unit and sign (line 46), so a metric can be quoted as a different quantity or the wrong sign. The guard reports all of these as grounded.
findings.repro: metrics M1=12 months, M2=264312.5, M5=-2300. guard.check grounded=True for: 'Stock is worth forty-eight thousand pounds.'; 'The owner says HMRC is owed 30 thousand.'; 'Cash reserves are £12 [M1] million.'; 'The lowest balance was a healthy £2,300 [M5] in credit.' (probe1.py case F)

findings.claim: The prompt requires the Recommendation to name the referred/failed rules, and each rule line passed to the model includes its threshold (policy.py:43, 'rule requires >= 1.25'). Thresholds are not metrics, so a real model that explains a referral naturally ('below the 1.5x refer band') is flagged, redrafted twice, and reaches the analyst marked ungrounded. Reviewers will learn to override. FakeLLM never quotes thresholds, so the 9/9 grounded evals cannot show this.
findings.repro: guard.check('Cover of 1.42x [M10] is below the 1.5x refer band and above the 1.25x minimum.', metrics incl. M10=1.42) -> grounded=False, unmatched ['1.5x','1.25x']. (probe1.py case F, last line)

findings.claim: The approved memo written to --out is memo text plus a stamp (graph.py:174). It has [Mn] tags but no metrics table, methods or evidence ids, and the M-ids are defined only in the in-memory MemorySaver state that is gone when the process exits. 'When compliance asks where a figure came from' cannot be answered from the artefact, which is the bet's outcome (b).
findings.repro: cma run examples/cafe_stretched.csv --yes --reviewer 'A. Analyst' --out memo.md; memo.md contains '[M3]' etc. and no table or transaction ids (compare examples/cafe_stretched.memo.md:1-19).

findings.claim: Only ISO dates in an oldest-first, BOM-free, signed-amount CSV are accepted. UK bank exports are typically DD/MM/YYYY, newest-first, often with separate paid-in/paid-out columns and an Excel BOM. All of these are refused. The bet's non-goals mention only CAMT/MT940, so the pilot will rely on an unwritten, unaudited manual reshaping step before the 'every figure is traced' chain starts.
findings.repro: Reverse rows of examples/cafe_stretched.csv -> StatementError with 385 problems ('running balance ... does not follow'). Same file saved as utf-8-sig -> 'missing column(s): id (found: \ufeffid, ...)'.

findings.claim: truth.lowest_balance starts at the opening balance, which is not a statement row, while M5 is the minimum over rows. P1 ('for any synthetic statement') fails; the tests only use seed 7.
findings.repro: synth.generate('trades','good',seed=1,end=date(2026,9,30)) -> M5=17327.55, truth.lowest_balance=14000.0 (also seeds 6 and 9). (probe1.py case H)

findings.claim: The default end date is date.today(), so `cma generate` with the same arguments produces a different statement, trend and policy outcome each month. This contradicts the docstring at synth.py:8.
min_length=1 counts whitespace, so a reviewer of '   ' is accepted as an identity by the review node and by `--yes --reviewer ' '` (cli.py:50 checks truthiness only).
The eval exit code depends only on M2 matching truth (line 58), and it exits 0 even when 0/9 memos are grounded. README.md:60 and ci.yml claim it fails CI 'if any metric disagrees with truth'.
findings.repro: Read run_evals.py:58 and :72; no other metric or grounding result affects the return code.

findings.claim: M4 compares the last three months with the first three, so it measures seasonality: trades/good is referred at -24.5% and ecommerce/good at -27.9%, while cafe/poor shows +18.5% growth. A first-three-month total of 0 gives 0.0 and passes R6. The limit is documented in the README, but policy R6 (policy/uk_sme_default.yaml:49) still acts on it, so the analyst will disagree with the outcome by design.
findings.repro: probe2.py: trades/good M4=-24.5 -> policy refer; cafe/poor M4=18.5.

findings.claim: Months are the distinct months that have transactions. A missing month is not detected, so a 13-month span with a gap still reports M1=12 and passes R1, and M3 divides by the months present.
findings.repro: Statement 2025-01..2026-01 with no 2025-03 rows -> M1=12, policy R1 pass; ingest raises nothing.

findings.claim: 'PARCELFORCE WORLDWIDE' is a real UK carrier, which contradicts 'Counterparties are fictional' (synth.py:23) and README.md:103. It is not customer data, so R8 still passes.
